correctness.rationale: The full proof derives the exact integer-polynomial representation, Vandermonde shift, prime-power valuations and recurrence minimality. For c even with valuation \(t\ge2\) it proves a unique lowest-valuation shift term, and for \(t=1\) it proves a cancelling pair at \(j=1,2\); each gives an exact dyadic least period. The c odd preperiod follows from a recurrence induction with explicit last nonzero residue. All cases combine by CRT. Independent finite recurrence and shift calculations through specified bounds corroborate but do not replace the unrestricted proof.

originality.rationale: The unweighted \(c=1\) case is already completely proved by Kim and Kim (2009), and the weighted odd-shift upper bounds are established by Bednarz and Wołowiec-Musiał (2019). The novelty claim is restricted to the new exact even-weight binary phase split and global all-integer-parameter synthesis: c divisible by 4 has universally sharp 2-adic shifts, whereas c congruent to 2 modulo 4 exhibits an additional two-term cancellation. These are absent from the full-text prior results inspected. Priority remains subject to unlocated specialized historical literature.
residual_risks: A specialized prior theorem on the Hermite/complete-graph matching polynomial at even edge weights could contain an equivalent minimal-period formula not found through the available searches.
The universal weighted-permutation congruence has wide scope, but no stronger unpublished or external specialization was established.
The \(c=1\) case and odd shift upper bounds are emphatically not original.

value.rationale: The exact least eventual period and preperiod of a natural weighted matching enumerator modulo every integer is an invariant that distinguishes parameter-driven arithmetic regimes. In particular, the unexpected \(c\equiv2\pmod4\) cancellation versus the sharp noncancellation for 4|c produces different dyadic period growth, and the exact shift valuation is stronger than merely bounding a period. The pre-existing \(c=1\) and odd-shift ingredients are transparently isolated; no unsupported downstream importance is claimed.
